text.p: -- UBS Securities analyst Edward Hatch said in a research note he lowered his rating on Scholastic Corp to hold from buy and lowered the fiscal 1997 earnings estimate to $1.60 per share from $3.30 and cut the fiscal 1998 outlook to $2.40 per share from $3.85.
-- Hatch said the downgrade was based on "unforseen book sales declines" at Scholastic's trade and club operations.

-- The earning estimate reductions were based on "substantial negative sales and margin impact. Goosebumps, a major new book franchise, saw sales unexpectedly slow and returns soar in the January period. Core book club business is now forecast to take longer to resume growth and promotional costs are high. Earnings visibility is materially reduced as is investor confidence. (We) see shares falling to mid-40s range," Hatch said.
-- In early Nasdaq trade, Scholastic shares were off 25 points, or 41 percent, to 36.
